name: Ripple

summary.text: Ripple Labs is a cryptocurrency company led by chief executive Brad Garlinghouse. FactCheck.org identifies it as one of the three largest contributors to the crypto super PAC Fairshake, with Coinbase and Andreessen Horowitz. It gave Fairshake $25 million in May 2024, announced another $25 million for the 2026 midterms in November 2024, and was reported to have given a further $25 million in the second half of 2025.

facts.claim: In late May 2024 Ripple gave $25 million to the Fairshake super PAC, as did Andreessen Horowitz; Coinbase followed with $25 million in early June 2024.
facts.quote: Coinbase donates $25 million to super PAC Fairshake days after Biden vetoes crypto custody bill

sources.title: Coinbase donates $25 million to super PAC Fairshake days after Biden vetoes crypto custody bill

facts.claim: On November 26, 2024 Brad Garlinghouse announced on X that Ripple would give another $25 million to Fairshake for the 2026 midterms. Decrypt described it as Ripple's third $25 million contribution in the past year and reported that Garlinghouse called Fairshake the most successful multi-candidate, bipartisan super PAC in U.S. history and said Ripple was contributing to keep up that momentum.

facts.claim: Yahoo Finance reported in early 2026, citing figures Fairshake shared with CNBC before the January 31 FEC deadline, that Fairshake held $193 million for the 2026 midterms and that $25 million from Ripple and $24 million from a16z came in the second half of 2025.

facts.claim: FactCheck.org identifies Coinbase, Ripple Labs and AH Capital Management (Andreessen Horowitz) as Fairshake's largest contributors. Wikipedia, citing FEC data, puts Ripple Labs' giving to Fairshake at $45 million; this figure should be checked against FEC filings.
The Washington Post reported that the Fairshake-network ads it viewed in the 2024 cycle did not mention crypto and that the super PACs were backed by Coinbase and Ripple.
facts.quote: none of the ads viewed by The Post actually mention crypto

openQuestions: Not recorded (search budget exhausted before sec.gov and court-coverage results were obtained): the SEC's December 2020 suit against Ripple, Judge Torres's July 2023 ruling, the August 2024 $125 million penalty, and the 2025 end of the case. No 'sec' connection is recorded for that reason.
Basic company facts (founding year, headquarters, private status) were not sourced in this run.

Ripple's total giving to Fairshake: $45 million for the 2024 cycle (Bloomberg Government analysis of FEC data as cited by Wikipedia and Cointelegraph); Decrypt counts three $25 million gifts in the year to November 2024; a Ripple executive was quoted by an aggregator saying November 2024 was the third time Ripple had donated. None of these was verified at the FEC.
Garlinghouse's November 2024 wording is recorded as reported by Decrypt, not as a direct quote, because the verbatim post was not captured.
